findings.passage: Their arithmetic is not uniformly correct: G1 notes quote \$198 for orange redemption rather than the implemented \$200, G1 quotes \$220 for Boardwalk rather than \$221, and G16 quotes \$110 for New York rather than \$111.
findings.evidence: Grok's three figures are the exact ten-percent redemption charges (2x99, 220, 110). The implemented charges come from engine.py _unmortgage_cost = int(math.ceil(value*1.1)), which overcharges by $1 for principals 50/90/100/110/200 (recomputed here and identical to Appendix C l.133). The delivered prompts never show a redemption charge. A census of all 6,989 initial prompts finds no price, cost, mortgage-value or redemption field in any POST_TURN_ACTION_DECISION (4,081). The G1 d298 tool description is only 'Unmortgage a property you own.' Grok therefore used the only charge it could know, and the discrepancy is the paper's own documented implementation overcharge, not model arithmetic. The sentence entered during integration from OPR-24/FX-C05. OPR-24 called $220 'the standard-rule figure', not an error.
findings.proposed_resolution: Replace with: 'Their redemption figures (\$198 for the two orange deeds, \$220 for Boardwalk, \$110 for New York) are the exact ten-percent charges; prompts do not display redemption costs, and the engine's floating-point ceiling charges \$200, \$221 and \$111 (Appendix~\ref{app:rules}). The table uses the implemented charges.' Also amend integration_decisions.md (OPR-24 and FX-C05 rows), which currently describe these as note rounding/arithmetic errors.
findings.check_status: performed (original-record/source read or retained-ledger re-tabulation; no engine, game or model execution)

findings.passage: Prompts show cash, ownership, buildings, bank stock, twenty public timeline entries and ten own private notes.
findings.evidence: Census of all 6,989 decision_started payloads (game_state without memory, plus action_state). BUY_OR_AUCTION_DECISION (547) carries price, house_cost, rent, group and group_progress for the landed deed. AUCTION_BID_DECISION (854) carries group. POST_TURN_ACTION_DECISION (4,081), TRADE_RESPONSE_DECISION (920), JAIL_DECISION (249) and LIQUIDATION_DECISION (338) carry none of these fields. Management, trade and liquidation menus list space keys only, with no sale, mortgage or redemption values. Every arithmetic claim the paper evaluates (G2 nine houses, G13 5/36 and Short Line distance, G15 $600 layer, G19 'States is the third orange', Grok redemption figures, G12/G17 omitted collateral) therefore rests on recalled standard-board parameters. The system prompt promises 'full board/game context'.
findings.proposed_resolution: Add after the first sentence of §2.4: 'Only purchase and auction prompts state the landed deed's price, house cost, rent schedule or color group. Management, trade-response and liquidation prompts list space keys and legal key menus without prices, rents, mortgage values, sale proceeds or redemption charges, so agents' valuations and arithmetic rely on recalled standard-board parameters.' Optionally add one row to the evidence map citing this census.

findings.passage: The hotel cannot be downgraded, and even-selling blocks a lower sibling's house. The mortgage-only continuation reaches \$440 and automatic bankruptcy, despite \$1,310 in nominal resources.
findings.evidence: The original G7 d339 request lists sellable_building_space_keys: [] and available_actions [mortgage_property, declare_bankruptcy]. In engine.py, _sellable_building_space_indices offers only a group's highest-built deeds and offers a hotel only when bank houses >= 4, so the menu is empty. _build_liquidation_decision then omits sell_houses_or_hotel. By contrast, _validate_sell_plan checks bank stock (houses_remaining + net delta >= 0) and evenness only after the whole plan. A plan clearing the group (St. Charles 4 houses, States 4 houses, Virginia hotel, Virginia 4 houses) would have net bank +8 houses and final 0/0/0, and would raise $650 (390+650 = 1,040 >= 750). Appendix C states the bundled-sale property and calls G7 a 'mortgage-only state' but never connects them. A reader of App C can conclude that a bundled sale pays the debt, so the main-text exception looks contradicted. This is a source-reading inference about acceptance; no plan was executed.
findings.proposed_resolution: State in §6.1 and App C that the lock is a property of the implemented liquidation menu: no sale action is offered, so no bundled plan can be submitted, although the plan validator alone would accept a group-clearing bundle. Optionally phrase the abstract as 'one is blocked by the implementation's hotel-sale menu despite sufficient nominal assets'. See replacement_prose.tex.
findings.check_status: performed (original-record/source read or retained-ledger re-tabulation; no engine, game or model execution); bundle acceptance is inferred from source, not executed

findings.passage: The systems complete 17, 18, 15 and 13 color groups through trade, but build on 16, 17, 7 and 3 in their first management windows. Construction gaps mix deferred financing, engine defaults and received actions conflicting with accompanying text. One participant receives action-only refusal recovery on 1,604 of 1,696 decisions.
findings.evidence: The abstract's lead result has unlabeled number vectors and an unnamed 'one participant'. first_management_windows.json summary gives the per-configuration residuals. Grok's ten are 4 no-option with stated deferral, 4 received-call conflicts and 2 stated holds. Opus's eight are 5 no-option windows (action-only, no private notes) and 3 defaults after refusal. Sol's one is a default. Gemini's one is a valid end. Only 4 of the 20 residuals carry a stated financing deferral, so 'deferred financing' over-describes the no-option category: 2 of 9 fall short even of the static mortgage budget, and 5 have no stated reason. The main text gives Opus's split (development.tex:34) but never Grok's, even though Grok has the lowest conversion.
findings.proposed_resolution: Name the systems in the abstract and replace the gap sentence (see replacement_prose.tex). Add one sentence to development.tex:6 giving the Grok and Opus residual splits.

findings.evidence: Same unquantified 'often' at temporal_discussion.tex:23 ('often after collecting rent on an already-developed group'). appendix.tex:92 has an orphan sentence: 'Fifty-seven developed-color rent elimination triggers concern events.' Recount from the original event streams, using the debtor's last move before each BANKRUPTCY marker: 57 of 60 eliminations follow landing on a developed color deed owned by the creditor, and 38 of the 40 nonterminal ones do.
